system.summary: The "Clave G.A." card (CMXV.16.1557.1 scans 12-13): a digraphic table of 2 rows x 15 columns; a plain letter is one of five row letters (WZCTG or MVPKI) followed by its column letter (BLRAFQENHDXYOSJ); the coded groups of a run are read together, two letters at a time. A different cipher from the "nueva clave" grille of 18-20 April (nuevaclave1911).

prior_solution.where: The key card "Clave G.A. (una de las usadas en San Antonio)", CMXV.16.1557.1 scans 12-13, in the same fonds; no decipherment of 1432.1-4 or 1561.7-13 on the sheet or in CMXV.18.1795.1. CMXV.17.1695.1-2 was deciphered at the time: the pencil gloss "Jose Pineda" on the form (the CEHM record 12896 prints the name, so it was known before the attempt) and the whole telegram in CMXV.18.1795.1, entry 113, which Daniel Jalkut found after the card had given josepinfda (PR #831).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout directed the work and decided what to publish. Claude (Opus) agents transcribed the card and the telegrams from the CEHM viewer images, ran the preregistered measure of the card and wrote the readings. An AI model (Claude Fable 5.2, one API run) pointed out that the coded groups of 1561.7-13 must be joined before they are cut into pairs. Daniel Jalkut (PR #831, with Claude Code) transcribed the two telegrams of 5 May 1911 (1695.1-2 and 1695.2-2) from the CEHM images, applied the card and found 1695.1-2 in the typed list CMXV.18.1795.1; the PR #831 review (an AI agent) compared 1695.1-2 and entry 113 with the CEHM images. No human palaeographer checked the transcriptions.

solution.what: Telegram and key card transcribed from the CEHM viewer images; hashed before any key was tried.

The "Clave G.A." card (CMXV.16.1557.1 scans 12-13) selected among the fonds' cards on the first half of the coded letters; it decodes all six coded words (Galeana, Dr, Ag, Guerrero, Chih, Encinillas), two pairs faulty in transmission.
First held-out measure on two telegrams: 30 letters, car 0.833 vs best control 0.667: too short, not validated.

Preregistered measure run once: the card as is against the period decipherments of eight sibling telegrams, cipher transcribed blind; agreement 0.866 on 769 cipher letters vs at most 0.257 for 400 controls (VALIDATION.md).
Reading checked as Spanish sentences: 19 of 20 words read as sense; Ag not identified.

1561.7-13 (19 April 1911) decoded with the same card once the coded groups are joined before cutting into pairs (an earlier group-by-group attempt failed): DR, CLAVE, FONDOS, PARQUE; all four coded words read.

Integration check by an independent session: own decoder from key.tsv reproduces the decryptions of both telegrams; the validation table of 28 segments gives A = 0.8655 (all 28 edit distances right), the contributor's 0.866; the scripts and the clear/cipher files of that test are kept outside the repository, so it was not re-run. Strict count by words (restored words not counted): 1432.1-4 18 of 20 = 90% (GALEANA and GUERRERO each need a faulty or lost pair repaired by the sense), 1561.7-13 21 of 21.
Housekeeping: The three telegrams in the turning grille moved out to nuevaclave1911 (one key, one entry): the card and the grille are different systems.
Daniel Jalkut (PR #831) transcribed CMXV.17.1695.1-2 and 1695.2-2 (5 May 1911) from the CEHM images, with eight other sibling telegrams of catalogue 1462 (files in ../duron1911/siblings/).
The Clave G.A. card on the four coded groups of 1695.1-2, joined and read in pairs: josepinfda (pL = f is a slip for e), the name José Pineda that the pencil gloss on the form gives.

The same card on the eight coded groups of 1695.2-2 (42 letters), at both offsets: only 'aton' (offset 1) and '...l..v..oucsenn?s' (offset 0), where the pencil gloss of the time also stops; no sentence.

The typed list CMXV.18.1795.1 searched by the contributor (45 scans, tesseract OCR, then the pages of the dates by eye): entry 113 is 1695.1-2 in full ('Nemi informa mercancías enviadas capitán Lewis decomisadas. Envíen facturas José Pineda para reclamarlas. Conviene llamen Lewis. Esperen carta.'); entry 114, right after it, is blank.

PR #831 review (an AI agent, two rounds): own decoder from key.tsv gives josepinfda and the two offsets of 1695.2-2 as filed; the four coded groups of 1695.1-2 and the pencil 'Jose Pineda' over them compared with the CEHM image; entry 113 seen on CEHM scan 21 word for word, entry 114 blank. 1695.2-2 was not compared with its image.

Integration of PR #831: 1695.1-2 (read from the decipherment of the time) and 1695.2-2 (decoded, not read) filed here (one key, one entry); their files stay in ../duron1911/siblings/ and are referenced; English of 1695.1-2 added as translation_1695-1-2.md. Own decode from key.tsv repeated, equal to the filed lines; scan 21 and the crop of the gloss looked at again.

validation.notes: The key is the archive's own card, not recovered here, so docs/_validate.py does not apply. The contributor's preregistered test of the card passed: A = 0.866 on 769 cipher letters of eight sibling telegrams against at most 0.257 for 400 controls (VALIDATION.md; recomputed from its table at 0.8655; the scripts are not in the repository).

outcome.method_basis: Both telegrams are read with the archive's own card "Clave G.A." (CMXV.16.1557.1 scans 12-13), applied unchanged and validated beforehand against the period decipherments of eight sibling telegrams (A = 0.866 on 769 cipher letters, controls at most 0.257; thresholds fixed in advance, passed). CMXV.17.1695.1-2 (part 2) is read from the decipherment of the time (pencil gloss and CMXV.18.1795.1 entry 113), which the card confirms; 1695.2-2 is decoded with the card, not read.

outcome.notes: Two telegrams read with the archive's Clave G.A. card; the card was validated beforehand on period decipherments of eight sibling telegrams (A = 0.866, passed). By the README rule (words) 39 of 41 = 95.1% over both, but 1432.1-4 alone is 18 of 20 = 90% (two words repaired by the sense), so the target is read in part; 1561.7-13 is read in full. The card's transcription is the contributor's, checked by no second reader. The three telegrams in the turning grille are on nuevaclave1911, a different cipher with its own page. Added 21 Nov 2026 from PR #831 (Daniel Jalkut): 1695.1-2 of 5 May 1911, read from the decipherment of the time (2 of 2 cipher words), and 1695.2-2, decoded, not read; neither is in the 39 of 41.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration count by words (README rule), from reading.md and reading_1561-7-13.md: 41 words, 39 read = 95.1% (1432.1-4 18 of 20 = 90%, GALEANA and GUERRERO restored by the sense; 1561.7-13 21 of 21). The contributor counts 19 of 20 for 1432.1-4. Not in this figure: 1695.1-2 (part 2, read from the decipherment of the time, 2 of 2 cipher words; these counts are of the whole telegrams, that one of cipher words only) and 1695.2-2 (decoded, not read).

texts.label: Telegram of 29 March 1911 to John McCarty (CEHM-Carso CMXV.15.1432.1-4)
texts.summary: González Garza at El Paso to Adolfo González at San Antonio: on the 13th Dr (probably Madero) and Ag separated at Galeana, one towards Guerrero, the other towards Chihuahua, camping on the 23rd at Encinillas.

reading_review.note: Read as Spanish sentences: the six decoded words fill the gaps of the clear text; two faulty pairs corrected by the sense, so by the README rule 18 of 20 words (90%).

texts.label: Telegram of 19 April 1911 to Adolfo González, Clave G.A. (CEHM-Carso CMXV.16.1561.7-13)
texts.summary: González Garza to Adolfo González: Dr wants Elías to come too; keep using the old key while the crisis lasts, it is quicker; send funds and ammunition of all kinds at once.

reading_review.note: All four coded words decode letter for letter with the validated card and complete the clear sentences.

texts.label: Telegram of 5 May 1911, J. González (Marfa) to W. Olliphant (CEHM-Carso CMXV.17.1695.1-2)
texts.summary: J. González at Marfa to González Garza (W. Olliphant) at El Paso: Nemi reports the goods sent by Captain Lewis seized; send the invoices with José Pineda to claim them back; call Lewis; a letter follows. The coded words are the name José Pineda.
texts.note: The siblings files of PR #831 hold ten telegrams: this entry is the block or section headed CMXV.17.1695.1-2 in each. Read from the decipherment of the time: the pencil gloss "Jose Pineda" over the four coded groups, and the whole telegram in the typed list CMXV.18.1795.1, entry 113. The card gives josepinfda (pL = f is a slip for e), so the card alone would leave Pineda with one corrected letter; the 2 cipher words are read from the decipherment.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #831 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: A name of two words in a clear sentence: 'Envíen facturas José Pineda para reclamarlas.' Checked: the four coded groups kopjg Ftskf Tlkap Lvnme and the pencil 'Jose Pineda' over them on the CEHM image (compared by the PR #831 review; the crop looked at again here); the whole telegram in the typed list CMXV.18.1795.1, entry 113, on CEHM scan 21, word for word as quoted (seen by the review and again here), and entry 114 blank; own decode from key.tsv gives josepinfda, equal to the filed decryption. Not checked: the clear words of the form beyond the crop of its two coded lines. A model's reading: no person has checked it.

texts.label: Telegram of 5 May 1911, "J. Gouzateo" (Presidio) to W. Olliphant (CEHM-Carso CMXV.17.1695.2-2)
texts.summary: A telegram from Presidio, 11:31 pm, in garbled clear Spanish about Luque and Mulato, with eight coded groups that the card turns into fragments only ('aton', '...oucsenn?s'), where the pencil decipherment of the time also stops.
texts.note: The block or section headed CMXV.17.1695.2-2 in the siblings files of PR #831. Entry 114 of CMXV.18.1795.1, right after 1695.1-2, is blank. The transcription was not compared with the image at the review.
